question: A Canadian home-maintenance note says “clean the eavestroughs.” Which part of the house does that refer to, and what other common word might a neighbour use?
generated_answer:
A very Canadian question!

In Canada, "eavestroughs" refers to the gutters on a house. Specifically, they are the channels or troughs that collect and direct rainwater and melting snow away from the foundation of the house.

A neighbour might use the more common word "gutters" to refer to the same thing. So, if someone says "clean the eavestroughs," you can respond with "oh, you mean clean the gutters?" and they'll know exactly what you're talking about!
